news.title: Xabi Alonso says Blues duo in contention to face Luton
news.body_en: Xabi Alonso has confirmed Danny Welbeck and Emmanuel Emegha could make their Chelsea debuts when we take on Luton Town in the second round of the Carabao Cup. The attacking duo didn’t feature in our final friendly, against Real Sociedad, nor our Premier League opener at Craven Cottage earlier in the week, when Welbeck was an unused substitute. Our manager had positive news on their fitness, but confirmed the game will come too soon for another new signing, Jordan Henderson. ‘Danny and Emma, yes [they will be in contention to face Luton],’ said Alonso. ‘Jordan will take a little bit longer. Let's see. I'm not a doctor and I don't have the data. We need to wait until we know more.' It is still early days for Alonso at Chelsea, but the early signs in our victory at Craven Cottage were very promising indeed. Our new manager knows there is plenty of work ahead to mould this Blues team in his image, but he is confident to see consistent progress as the campaign unfolds. 'Most of the teams will get better and better in the weeks ahead and with more games,’ said Alonso. ‘We have some players that have just been back for two weeks, they are in good shape but they will get better. 'There are teams that have been working longer with their manager and so many ideas are already very established. With other projects, in different cases, it takes more time. So there will be a development of many concepts. 'As I said in another press conference, I think that we started our season Monday and the way we will be playing in January will be different. And I think it's going to be better, and the next year will be even better.'

news.title: Chelsea learn potential Carabao Cup third round opponents
news.body_en: Should we progress past Luton Town in the Carabao Cup tomorrow, we will play at Stamford Bridge in the third round of the competition. The draw was made after Everton’s victory at Preston North End and it handed Xabi Alonso’s side a potential tie against Leeds United, who defeated Nottingham Forest in the second round. It would be our third League Cup tie against Leeds, following victories in 1970, 2001 and, most memorably, 2012, when we won 5-1 at Elland Road. Third-round ties will be split across two midweek slots to accommodate European fixture commitments, with games played on the weeks beginning 7 September and 14 September. Should we beat Luton, fixture and ticket details will follow in due course.

news.title: Camille Abily praises attack and gives fitness update on Naomi Girma
news.body_en: Chelsea assistant coach Camille Abily hailed our wealth of resources in attack as our new number nine Melvine Malard scored a brace on her debut in our 5-2 win over Real Sociedad at Plough Lane on Wednesday. The striker combined with former Lyon teammate Ellie Carpenter for her second of the evening, the pair having worked under Abily and head coach Sonia Bompastor at the French club in the past. ‘They know each other really well,’ said Abily, who was deputising on the touchline for the suspended Bompastor. ‘They also get on really well. They speak in French sometimes, so it helps because no one understands. ‘It would be great anytime we are able to score five goals. Of course, we have quality on the pitch, and also on the bench, because today the subs helped the team a lot. ‘Up front, we have Melvine. We have Mayra (Ramirez). She's not here yet, but I hope she will be soon. Aggie (Beever-Jones) is able to play this position. Last year, Lauren James played in this position. ‘That wasn't what we wanted, but when we are missing forwards sometimes we need it. Melvine is really versatile. She's able to play different positions and Aggie also, so it can help the team.’ Sociedad took the lead after just seven minutes, and fought back to level the scores at 2-2 before we extended our lead in the latter stages of the contest. Abily paid tribute to the opposition, and explained some of the half-time tactical tweaks she made to turn the performance around. ‘It was a tough game,’ she said. ‘Especially in the first half because Real Sociedad are a really great team, but I think we had a good reaction. We were so much better in the second half. There was also more space for us. So a tough win, but a good win. ‘At half-time we said we wanted to find and play in the spaces behind because their back line was really high. We score many goals like this, so this is sort of what we want to do, so it was good. ‘It was a good experience on the touchline. It was fun, but it's okay. Sonia can take the spot again!’ Finally, the assistant coach explained why defender Naomi Girma was replaced by Lucy Bronze in the second half. ‘It's more fitness,’ she said. ‘And also a decision because we have many good players on the bench, and we know with her calf we need to be careful. So for that, we didn’t want to take any risks.'

Match Report: Chelsea 5-2 Real Sociedad
news.body_en: Melvine Malard scored a brace on her Chelsea debut as we battled back to take a 5-2 advantage into the second leg of our Women's Champions League qualifier with Real Sociedad. It soon became apparent that Real Sociedad would not be easy to overcome as Ainhoa Marin scored with a stunning looping strike after just seven minutes. Naomi Girma then put us back on even ground with a header from a Katie McCabe corner, but the Blues went in at the interval with the scores locked at 1-1. The second half saw Chelsea emerge with renewed vigour, Sjoeke Nusken seeing her attempt ruled out for offside before young defender Veerle Buurman rose up to deliver a powerful header across the line soon afterwards. Our Spanish visitors fought back almost immediately, Cecilia Marcos' strike putting Sociedad back on even terms. That Sociedad were so determined made what happened next all the more impressive. An inch-perfect through-ball from Nusken picked out Melvine Malard, allowing her to slot home on her debut. Next came a wonderful run from Ellie Carpenter down the right as she then picked out Lauren James in the box and the forward made no mistake with her emphatic finish. An exceptional evening in Wimbledon concluded with our fifth goal. Carpenter once again powered down the flank, delivering a cross for Malard, who marked her first competitive appearance in Blue in some style. Head coach Sonia Bompastor was serving a suspension for this match, leaving assistant Camille Abily to take charge of the team. And the match began with Chelsea in firm control of possession and dictating the tempo of play. Yet, after captain for the evening Naomi Girma had confidently shepherded a through-ball into touch, it was the Spanish side who took the lead thanks to a moment of brilliance from Ainhoa Marin. The Sociedad number eight received the ball on the corner of the penalty area, lofting it over the outstretched Hannah Hampton before the ball nestled perfectly in the far corner, putting the visitors ahead with only seven minutes on the clock. Chelsea still had plenty of attacking intent, and Sandy Baltimore was unlucky not to level the scores when she smashed an attempt onto the underside of the crossbar. The woodwork then came to the rescue for the Blues at the opposite end when Sociedad fired another dangerous shot towards goal, but the offside flag soon went up. The equaliser came from a well-worked set piece. McCabe, on her full debut for the Blues, took the inswinging corner for captain Girma to flick the ball up and over the goalkeeper with a header with 30 minutes gone. Moments later, the Blues almost went ahead when Aggie Beever-Jones received the ball in space inside the box, but she dragged her shot just wide of the left-hand post. The Spanish side were providing a real test: well-organised, positionally disciplined and working hard to keep us at bay. For that reason, Chelsea went in at 1-1 when the half-time whistle blew, and there was more work to be done after the interval. Shortly after the restart, Sjoeke Nusken had the ball in the back of the net, but the flag was raised to swiftly rule it out.  And when James took a dangerous corner-kick, Buurman rose high above every player inside the box to nod down a pinpoint header to put us ahead for the first time in the contest. But that lead would last just four minutes when Marcos rifled in a right-footed effort from inside the box, and the scores were tied once more. Chelsea weren't done, though. When Wieke Kaptein laid the ball off for Nusken 20 yards from goal, the Germany international played a perfect through ball for debutant Melvine Malard, allowing the France international to round the goalkeeper and slot home. There was a sense that Real Sociedad were tiring, and when Carpenter powered down the line, her defender slipped at the crucial moment, allowing the Australian to pull the ball back for the onrushing James, who finished emphatically under the crossbar. Chelsea were now in the ascendancy, and substitute Maika Hamano was inches away from connecting with a pass that would've given the goalkeeper a stern test with ten to play. Taking a two-goal lead into the second leg would've been good enough, but an almost carbon-copy of James' goal extended our advantage even further. Carpenter advanced down the channel again, her pace beating her marker, when she squared the ball across the box for former-Lyon team-mate Malard. Our new number nine had a brace on her debut, a sure sign of things to come from the striker. We head into the second leg in San Sebastian on Wednesday 2 September with a three-goal cushion. We travel to Spain to face the return leg of this Women's Champions League qualifier against Real Sociedad, before we face Aston Villa at home on Saturday 5 September at Stamford Bridge, our first Women's Super League clash of the season. You can purchase your tickets for that exciting home game here. news.body_en: Chelsea take a 5-2 advantage into the second leg of our Women's Champions League qualifier against Real Sociedad, but who was your standout performer? news.title: Under-18 Premier League Cup report: Wolverhampton Wanderers 0-2 Chelsea
news.body_en: Chelsea Under-18s began our U18 Premier League Cup campaign with a 2-0 victory over Wolverhampton Wanderers, as goals from Andrew Pennie and Heze Grimwade secured the win at the Sir Jack Hayward Training Ground. The Blues pressed with purpose from the opening stages and Pennie provided an early breakthrough with a powerful right-footed finish. Wolves continued to threaten, but Chelsea defended well when called upon and goalkeeper Jake Murray produced an important second-half save. Substitute Grimwade then doubled our advantage with 14 minutes remaining to complete the scoring. Chelsea created the first opportunity after five minutes. Yunus Linton's pressing presented Pennie with a chance in front of goal, but Alfie Arnold made the save. The breakthrough followed shortly afterwards. Pennie charged into the penalty area before beating Arnold with a powerful right-footed effort from a tight angle. Linton was among those to test the Wolves goalkeeper, directing a left-footed attempt towards the centre of the goal in the 38th minute, but Arnold kept it out. The hosts threatened at the other end moments later. Emmanuel Ayinde applied the defensive pressure required to prevent the Wolves striker from going through one-on-one. Pennie had the final opportunity of the half, sending a firm right-footed effort from outside the penalty area narrowly wide of the right post. The Blues continued to threaten after the interval and Linton forced another save with a left-footed strike in the 58th minute. Dan Hogan made three changes on the hour, introducing Trey Faromo-Adebayo, Grimwade and Bilal Shah in place of Linton, Pennie and Jack Anderson. Gabriel Sambou and Diego Chinyowa followed shortly afterwards. Wolves then applied a quick spell of pressure and Murray was called into action in the 71st minute. Our goalkeeper produced an excellent save to deny a close-range effort and protect Chelsea's advantage. Grimwade saw a shot blocked after receiving a good pass into the box from Shah, but the substitute was not to be denied. A minute later, Grimwade found space at a tight angle inside the penalty area and produced a composed right-footed finish to double the Blues' lead. The result gives Chelsea three points from our opening U18 Premier League Cup fixture of the 2026/27 season, to join Manchester United on maximum points in Group F. Our Under-18s return to league action on Saturday 29 August, when we host Reading at Cobham Training Centre. The fixture kicks off at 11am and can be watched live with a CFC+ subscription. news.title: Confirmed Chelsea Women line up vs Real Sociedad
news.body_en: Sonia Bompastor has named her first starting XI of the 2026/27 campaign, with the Blues facing Real Sociedad in the Women's Champions League third qualifying round first leg at Plough Lane. Our third-place finish in the Women's Super League last term means we will play this qualifier against the Spanish side to determine whether or not we enter the league phase of this season's Women's Champions League. The match will be played over two legs, with the second fixture at the Estadio Zubieta in San Sebastian scheduled for 2 September at 6pm. Blues head coach Sonia Bompastor has named defender Naomi Girma as her skipper for the evening, while summer signing Katie McCabe comes straight into the starting XI. Fellow arrivals Giulia Dragoni, Nelly Las and Melvine Malard all make the substitutes' bench, and Manaka Matsukubo misses out through injury as Bompastor confirmed in her pre-match press conference. news.title: Alonso on a balancing act and team focus
news.body_en: Xabi Alonso explained why it will be vital for him to find the right balance to his team to face Luton Town on Thursday evening. Chelsea’s Carabao Cup campaign kicks off in west London tomorrow night, when we host League One side Luton in Alonso’s first competitive match on home soil in the Stamford Bridge dugout. Ahead of the second round tie, our Spanish manager was asked if he is likely to rotate his starting XI for this knockout game. It comes hot on the heels of Monday’s 3-2 win at Fulham in our opening Premier League fixture of the season, with the league visit of Brighton & Hove Albion fast approaching on Sunday. Alonso insisted he won’t be taking our Carabao Cup opponents lightly, ensuring that any rotation retains the right balance and competitiveness in the Chelsea line-up, as he plots our progress across three domestic fronts this season. ‘This season, knowing that we have time for all the competitions, every cup is important, every game is important,’ insisted Xabi. ‘We want to have the best competitive team to face Luton, with all the respect that everything deserves. And Luton are going to be the first game in the Carabao Cup. ‘The main thing is the quality of the players, that they adjust and that we have balance with the players around them that makes sense and makes the team better. ‘That is always my main focus, that the team is better with the qualities and knowing the best qualities of each individual player.’ During his pre-match press conference ahead of the Carabao Cup second round meeting with Luton, Alonso was also asked if he offered any specific words for Robert Sanchez in the last couple of days. It is clear that it is the team’s performance which is foremost in the mind of manager and players. ‘No, normal conversations,’ our manager responded. ‘We have talked more about team things, what we did well, what we have to do better. It was more about understanding the context of the game. ‘Every game is going to be important because we are in this process where we need to develop things, we need to make adjustments and we are more team focused.’

news.title: Xabi Alonso delivers the latest Chelsea team news ahead of Luton
news.body_en: Xabi Alonso confirmed at his pre-match press conference that both Moises Caicedo and Marco Palestra will miss Thursday’s Carabao Cup clash with Luton Town. The duo were both absent against Fulham on opening day, a game that the Blues won 3-2, and Alonso has announced that they will again sit out on Thursday - but Caicedo could return for the weekend visit of his former side Brighton. Elsewhere, the Spaniard stated that goalkeeper Mike Penders has an opportunity to feature, while he also expects Enzo Fernandez to be in the squad. ‘Not for tomorrow, both won’t make it [against Luton],’ Alonso said of Caicedo and Palestra. ‘Let’s see, hopefully Moi could make it for the weekend, but we need to check a little bit more with Marco. ‘Otherwise everyone from Monday is okay, Cole [Palmer] is absolutely fine. ‘Penders is part of the squad, so he has an opportunity. We will decide and then I am giving the team tomorrow to the players, so I prefer to respect that they know first. ‘Enzo, yes we expect him to be involved. He is training really well, he’s a good professional, and he will be involved.’

news.title: Chelsea vs Luton: Key statistics and facts
news.body_en: Chelsea begin our Carabao Cup campaign at the second-round stage, with a tie against League One Luton Town. Here are all the facts and figures you need ahead of the Hatters' visit to Stamford Bridge. Chelsea meet Luton Town for the first time since December 2023. Chelsea and Luton have never met in the League Cup before. We have faced them five times in the FA Cup, winning four, while our only Full Members’ Cup meeting ended in defeat on penalties. 	The Blues have won our past five meetings with Luton, starting with the 1994 FA Cup semi-final at Wembley. We then beat the Hatters in the FA Cup in both 2021 and 2022, before completing a Premier League double over them in 2023/24.	Luton’s last win at Stamford Bridge was 3-1 in September 1986 in the old First Division. Kerry Dixon scored our goal in front of just over 13,000 fans. Thursday’s game will be Chelsea’s 107th League Cup match at Stamford Bridge, having won 69 per cent of the previous 106 (five after a penalty shootout). Chelsea lost our most recent Carabao Cup home match, against Arsenal in last season’s semi-final first leg. Our previous defeat at Stamford Bridge in the competition came against Manchester United in 2019. If the aggregate scores are level after 90 minutes, the tie will be decided on penalties as there is no extra time in this competition until the semi-final stage. news.title: Axel Disasi completes Crystal Palace loan switch
news.body_en: Chelsea defender Axel Disasi has joined Crystal Palace on loan for the 2026/27 season. The centre-back moved to Stamford Bridge from AS Monaco in August 2023 and has made more than 60 appearances in blue. The France international started our first eight matches in the victorious UEFA Conference League campaign in 2024/25, before finishing the season on loan at Aston Villa. Disasi then spent the second half of last season on loan at West Ham, starting 16 of their 17 matches in all competitions. Everyone at Chelsea wishes Axel well and looks forward to following his progress during his time with Crystal Palace.

news.title: Chelsea's fastest Premier League goals 💥
Chelsea’s fastest Premier League goals
news.body_en: Joao Pedro gave Chelsea an early lead inside the first minute at Fulham, adding his name to the list of the Blues’ fastest scorers in the Premier League. The Brazilian opened the scoring with just 31 seconds on the clock at Craven Cottage on Monday night, breaking clear from Cole Palmer’s flick to make a flying start to the 2026/27 campaign and set us on our way to a 3-2 victory. It was officially the earliest goal ever on the Premier League’s opening weekend, but only good enough to come sixth on the all-time list of Chelsea’s fastest goalscorers in that competition. Here are the five players who found the net quicker for the Blues in the Premier League… Chelsea blew Man Utd away on Jose Mourinho’s return to Stamford Bridge with the Red Devils. It was Pedro who got the ball rolling on the thrashing when the visiting defenders dawdled in a moment of miscommunication. There was no such hesitancy from our Spanish forward, who took full advantage to round the keeper and slot in. It wasn’t to be Chelsea’s day, as Arsenal came back to take the win at Stamford Bridge and go seven points clear at the top of the Premier League table, but we had got off to the best possible start. That came when Gudjohnsen showed his instincts in the box to control Geremi’s cross brilliantly and fire the opening goal past the keeper. Manchester United’s run of 29 games without defeat came to an emphatic end at Stamford Bridge, as Chelsea turned on the style. The Blues went on the attack right from kick-off, giving Dan Petrescu the chance to cross. When United goalkeeper Massimo Taibi came to collect but collided with one of his defenders, Poyet gratefully headed into the empty net. The Blues were heavy favourites against newly-promoted Nottingham Forest when we met at the Bridge early in the 1998/99 campaign, despite the visitors' decent start to the season. We underlined that status early on, though, with a goal all of Zola’s own making. It was his cross into the box from a throw-in on the left which created the chance. When Forest failed to clear their lines, the Italian was there following in on his own cross to place a first-time finish into the bottom corner. Chelsea had lost two home games in a row when Leicester came to Stamford Bridge looking to be the next visiting side to inflict pain on the Blues. This time we raced into an early, and unassailable, lead. An early foul gifted us a free-kick on the halfway line and Dennis Wise took the chance to run clear into space. He then picked out a teasing angled cross to the back post, where Spencer floated in the air to meet it and head down into the net.

Chelsea and FPT extend strategic partnership into 2026/27 season
news.body_en: Chelsea Football Club and Global Technology Services provider FPT Corporation today announce the extension of our existing partnership for the 2026/27 season. Since first joining forces in 2025, Chelsea and FPT have worked closely together to transform the club’s digital capabilities and enhance the club’s fan engagement to bring Chelsea fans across the world closer to club. With FPT’s market-leading technology solutions and expertise, together Chelsea and FPT have delivered on a number of key projects. Megastore Express – a new mobile-first click-and-collect system – was unveiled in January and streamlines the retail experience for fans on matchdays. A new Official Supporters Club platform was also launched earlier this year and has become the new home for fans from across the world to build supporter groups, join in club activities and be a part of the Chelsea community. news.title: PGA South League report: London City Under-21s 0-8 Chelsea Women’s Under-18s
news.body_en: Chelsea Women’s Under-18s began their Professional Game Academy South League campaign in impressive fashion, securing an 8-0 victory away at London City Lionesses Under-21s on Wednesday evening. Chelsea Women's Under-18s, who play in the PGA Under-21 Women's League, were ahead inside seven minutes on Wednesday through Stevie Sinclair and established a two-goal advantage before the interval thanks to Maisie Brickell's strike. After the break, Chelsea added six more goals, with Chelsea N'Drin, Sinclair and Brickell all ending the match with two goals, while Jahyma Putman and Tess Finn also added their names to the scoresheet. Chelsea dominated possession throughout and combined attacking quality with defensive discipline to ensure they opened the new league season with both three points and a clean sheet. Chelsea made a positive start and moved in front after seven minutes. Victoria Rudz's clipped pass into the wide channel allowed Brickell to advance down the flank and deliver a cross into the box. Sinclair arrived from midfield and fired home from the edge of the area to give the Blues an early lead. The second goal arrived after 17 minutes and again involved Rudz and Brickell. Spotting space beyond the London City back line, Rudz played forward into the right channel, where Brickell drove towards goal before cutting across her defender and finishing at the near post. Chelsea continued to control possession and territory for the remainder of the first half, limiting opportunities for the hosts while taking a deserved two-goal advantage into the interval. A triple substitution at the break helped maintain Chelsea's momentum and a third goal arrived six minutes into the second half. After Putman switched play to Zoe Ciccardini, the defender found Sinclair's run in behind. The goalkeeper showed bravery to deny Sinclair's initial effort, but N'Drin reacted quickest to convert the rebound. Chelsea continued to press aggressively and nearly extended the lead further when N'Drin was brought down in the penalty area after a high regain. Sinclair's resulting penalty was saved, but the Blues were adding to the scoresheet once again soon after. The fourth goal arrived on 76 minutes when combinations around the edge of the box by Finn and N’Drin helped create space for Sinclair, who took a touch beyond the last defender before finishing confidently. A minute later Chelsea struck again. Finn recovered possession high up the pitch and switched play to Putman, who advanced towards goal before spinning past the goalkeeper and calmly finishing into an empty net. Finn then added her own name to the scoresheet on 86 minutes. After some quick combinations the ball was worked wide to Putman at left wing, she showed positive 1v1 play to get to the byline to pull the ball back to the edge of the box for the arriving Finn, who’s placed shot to the goalkeeper’s right added another. Three minutes later, N’Drin and Gregory helped win possession high up the pitch and the latter played into Brickell on the edge of the box. She turned and placed a composed finish across goal for Chelsea's seventh. There was still time for one more. Deep into added time, Sinclair dropped low to combine with Ciccardini, who was able to find Storey inside the pitch, with good vision and quick play. Storey played forward through the defensive line of London City Lionesses to find Brickell in the wide area. After some more positive play, Brickell delivered a lofted cross into the box which was met by N’Drin in the air to score the final goal. The result means Chelsea Women Under-18s sit top of the Professional Game Academy South League table thanks to their eight-goal winning margin. Chelsea's next fixture sees us travel to face Wycombe Wanderers Women in the senior Women's National League Cup on Thursday. The Blues then return to Professional Game Academy South League action on Sunday 30 August when Crystal Palace visit. news.title: EFL Trophy: Bristol Rovers 2-2 Cobham Next Gen (2-4 on pens)
news.body_en: Cobham Next Gen showed real heart as we came from two goals down to beat Bristol Rovers on penalties in our opening EFL Trophy fixture. The hosts led at the interval through Mees Rijks and extended their advantage via Joe Quigley shortly before the hour mark, despite the Blues enjoying most of the possession. Sol Gordon then created Harrison Bettoni’s 71st-minute goal before Chizaram Ezenwata drew us level in the closing stages. Freddy Bernal had kept Chelsea in the contest with several important saves and denied Jack Sparkes during the shoot-out, before Justin Osagie scored the decisive spot-kick to help us secure two points and go top in Southern Group C. Gordon had the first sight of goal after eight minutes, letting fly from the right side of the penalty area but sending his effort wide. Bernal produced a couple of important early saves to keep the contest close, but Bristol Rovers opened the scoring in the 22nd minute. Ryan de Havilland played the ball forward to Jack Aitchison, whose pass across goal was converted by Rijks. Chelsea had an opportunity to respond soon afterwards when Gordon won possession from Sparkes and found Ezenwata, but the forward was unable to take the chance. Harry Hudson made a double change in the 56th minute, introducing Lewi Richards and Mahdi Nicoll-Jazuli in place of Calvin Diakite and Harrison McMahon. Two minutes later, a cross the Blues were unable to clear reached Quigley at the far post and the striker finished to double the hosts’ advantage. Chelsea, who saw Andrew Pennie replace Jashayde Greenwood shortly after the hour mark, reduced the deficit in the 71st minute. Gordon beat Sparkes and drove to the byline before cutting the ball back for Bettoni, who finished first time. Bettoni found space again soon afterwards and went close to an equaliser. That second goal arrived in the 82nd minute. Nicoll-Jazuli’s neat spin created the opening and Ezenwata found the corner to bring the Blues level. Chelsea went in search of the winner and Pennie struck the side-netting in the second minute of stoppage time but the contest went to penalties. Ezenwata and Bettoni converted spot-kicks to help the Blues go 2-1 ahead, after Bernal saved from Sparkes. Richards then scored to make it 3-2 in the shootout and when Richard Smallwood failed to convert, it left Osagie to calmly seal a 4-2 shoot-out victory. Cobham Next Gen begin our EFL Trophy campaign with two points, earning one for the draw after 90 minutes and securing the bonus point through our shoot-out success. news.title: Key talking points from Bompastor and Bronze ahead of Real Sociedad
news.body_en: Sonia Bompastor and Lucy Bronze faced the media at Cobham this afternoon ahead of our Women's Champions League qualifier clash against Real Sociedad on Wednesday night. The Blues are looking to gain an advantage in the first leg at home in our maiden match at the Cherry Red Records Stadium, before heading to Spain for the return leg on 2 September. Tickets are still available for Wednesday's game, and you can purchase them here. Alongside the latest injury news provided by Bompastor, here is a rundown of the other major talking points from today's press conference... Sonia Bompastor: It will be a strong test. Real Sociedad finished third in the Liga F. They are a Spanish team, so they have a really strong philosophy in possession, but they have a lot of quality out of possession as well. We know everything about them now, and we prepared for the game well. But the game tomorrow will also be about us, and I'm confident with the quality we have shown during pre-season. Lucy Bronze: I remember playing against Real Sociedad in Liga F when I was at Barcelona, and they were always a good team. They always played good football. We had good results against them, but I always remember them being a really good team, something that me and Keira (Walsh) both spoke about recently. I actually watched the game last year when they were playing against Barca. They defended really well, which isn't the easiest thing to do against Barca when they were continually attacking. SB: Pre-season has been really good. We have worked really hard with a lot of intensity in training sessions. We travelled all over the world, and it was a really good opportunity for the squad to be together and for us to get to know each other better. Since we came back, we also recovered really well from the travel, but we got back to business, and I think we are in a really good place for the game tomorrow. LB: We've got a lot of young, talented players at Chelsea, a lot of eager players who are keen to learn and to listen. Sometimes they get things wrong, but they try really hard, and it's exciting to be part of the club and to see so many players grow, develop and improve every day. I think that's the exciting part of this team this year: the youth and the exuberance we will have on the pitch. LB: I think it's fun. We like playing against teams from different countries. The league phase last year was different, and I guess this is just another difference, but we're very much focused on this game. We know it's very important for us to win tomorrow, especially playing at home. We don't take anything for granted. We know what a good team they are. I think having more games this year is exciting for us as Chelsea, and being in a different position just allows you to adapt and learn new things about the team. LB: People forget how much spotlight was put on her from a very young age. But I think in the team at Chelsea, you can see she feels comfortable. She's grown as a player. She's grown as a person. You can see that she's grown so many connections with all of the team. We all know that when LJ is flowing, there's nobody in the world that can stop her. So it's nice to see that she's growing a lot. SB: As a coach, I'm someone who really cares about the players, but as a human, I also care about the humans and the person. So I think in this environment, I always try my best to encourage the players to be themselves and to express themselves. It's okay for us to be vulnerable sometimes. We spend so much time together, so I'm happy with what Lucy said in terms of allowing people to be themselves, in terms of vulnerability, but also when they are showing confidence, it's something good. LB: Pre-season has gone so well. The new signings are fitting in really well too. It just feels like we're on a fresh start. We have kind of put a line in the sand from last season, and moving forward to be even bigger and better than Chelsea's ever been. news.title: Rogers in focus 🔎
Analysis: How POTM Cole Palmer inspired Blues to victory
news.body_en: We detail the pivotal role Cole Palmer played in helping the Blues get our Premier League campaign up and running with a victory at Fulham. Our No10 was at his very best at Craven Cottage. Palmer assisted and scored a goal in the same Premier League game for the first time since February’s draw with Leeds United, with his cute finish early in the second half ultimately settling the contest. That was one of a game-high five attempts Palmer registered against Fulham, while he also led the way for successful dribbles (five), duels won (10), touches in the opposition box (nine) and fouls won (three). All those statistics point to the intent and confidence with which Palmer played. His nine attempted take-ons showed just how keen he was to beat his man, with one twisting and turning run in the second half nearly culminating in a special solo strike. Xabi Alonso’s system, using Palmer in a pocket alongside Morgan Rogers and off Joao Pedro, helped our No10 receive the ball. He spent more time in possession than every Chelsea outfielder bar Reece James, Josh Acheampong and Morgan Lacroix. Palmer was consistently effective when he had the ball at his feet. His assist for Joao Pedro’s record-breaking goal – the fastest ever scored in the Premier League on an opening weekend – was one of three key passes Palmer played, a figure bettered only by Rogers’ five. In total, Palmer completed 88 per cent of his passes, significantly higher than the team average of 82 per cent. A significant proportion (14) were played in the final third, too, highlighting his willingness to take risks. The weight and direction of Palmer’s passes were pivotal to our first and second goals, while his own strike showed his pinpoint accuracy in front of goal. The angle was narrow, so he aimed to slip the ball through Bernd Leno’s legs – and succeeded. Palmer wasn’t afraid to do his defensive work, either. He won two tackles and recovered possession seven times, including on three occasions in the final third. Those high turnovers proved instrumental for our first two goals of the night. Palmer was ably assisted by Joao Pedro and Rogers. That trio played 20 passes between them and showed signs of an understanding that bodes very well for the future – as does Palmer’s elite display. The Blues head coach was joined by Lucy Bronze on Tuesday afternoon to answer the media’s questions ahead of our opening fixture of the 2026/27 campaign, which takes place at the Cherry Red Records Stadium in Wimbledon. Bompastor will hope to see her side establish a lead ahead of the second leg in Spain next week, but she will not be able to call upon Erin Cuthbert, Mayra Ramirez and Manaka Matsukubo. ‘We have a squad with almost everyone pretty available from pre-season,’ said Bompastor. ‘The ones who are not available are Erin Cuthbert, who had an injury in the last international break and she's recovering from that. We also have Manaka, who won't be available for this game, and Mayra as well, who won't be available for the game. ‘I don't think we could expect to see them for the second leg. I think it'll be a little bit longer, but it's difficult to put a timeframe on it. They are working really well and progressing as we want them to progress, but yeah, no timeframe. ‘Except from these three, everyone else is available.’ Bompastor expanded on Ramirez’s recovery following the serious hamstring injury she suffered this time last year, with the head coach explaining her absence on Wednesday is expected. ‘Mayra is recovering from not having played last season, and I think it's tough sometimes when you haven't played for the full season to be ready to compete. ‘It's part of her rehab plan. She's not quite ready, but we are working closely with her to make sure she returns on the pitch as fit as possible.’

news.title: Joao Pedro on joining Palmer and Rogers in a ‘special’ front three
news.body_en: Joao Pedro believes Chelsea showed our strength in an impressive opening game of what could be a great season for the Blues, especially with the Brazilian lining up alongside Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers in a new-look attack. The starting line-up for Xabi Alonso’s first competitive match as Chelsea manager featured a front three of Joao Pedro down the middle, supported either side by Palmer and summer signing Rogers. It proved a big hit on its first outing, with all three of those players getting on the scoresheet as we began our 2026/27 campaign with a 3-2 Premier League win away at neighbours Fulham on Monday evening. That front three is already causing plenty of excitement among the Blues supporters following its debut at Craven Cottage, and it seems to be shared by Joao Pedro after a performance full of movement and clever combinations. ‘Cole and Morgan, they are special players. Everyone knows that,’ said Joao Pedro after Chelsea’s winning start to the season. ‘I'm very grateful to play with them because I know if I make some runs, like yesterday, you know Cole and Morgan are going to give the ball to me, and I have to be ready to score. So it's very special for me to play with them. ‘I just try to enjoy and try to help my team in every game. Then this season, see what I get. I just try to score in every opportunity I have. ‘I’ve known Morgan since a long time ago because we played against each other,' added our new number nine. 'So when he joined the club, I knew it was very good for us because he's a very good player, and I think he can help us like he did yesterday. ‘I think now in the game, if we move a lot, it will be difficult for defenders to pick up one player, to stay with them. The manager led us to be free on the pitch, so we understand each other well. So this just helps us and hopefully it can happen many more times this season.’ The striker was quick to point out the victory was down to the whole team’s display, though, not just that of the front three. Furthermore, he believes it was a performance and result which laid down a marker for the season to come. ‘I think the whole group was very good, we tried to do our job,’ he continued. ‘We conceded two goals, but I think we did a great game. It's very difficult to play there and get the three points, and that is the important thing. ‘I think it's too early to say what our target is, but we need to go step-by-step. We have to focus on the Premier League and the cups. We have a lot of time to train as well, to know what the coach wants from us. Let's see in the end, hopefully we can achieve our targets. ‘I will enjoy this season, of course, because I think we can achieve higher things. When you play for Chelsea, you always need to look for that. Yesterday was a great game to show our power and hopefully we can continue like this in the rest of the season.’ Up next is our midweek Carabao Cup clash against Luton Town and Alonso's Premier League home debut against Brighton & Hove Albion. news.title: Alonso explains how Palmer, Joao Pedro and Rogers can lead and inspire
news.body_en: Fulham discovered exactly what the attacking trio Cole Palmer, Joao Pedro and Morgan Rogers of are capable of at Craven Cottage on Monday evening. It was far less of a surprise for Blues manager Xabi Alonso, who believes the trio can inspire their Chelsea team-mates throughout the campaign. Palmer’s qualities are well known to Chelsea supporters; the 24-year-old has showcased them throughout his time at Stamford Bridge. Joao Pedro, who scored 20 goals and was named Player of the Season, has also demonstrated his talents on countless occasions. Rogers’ addition came earlier this summer and he has needed little time to adapt to life at Chelsea. Alonso deployed the three from the start against Fulham. Within 31 seconds, Palmer had teed up Joao Pedro to open the scoring. Rogers then opened his account in blue – sweeping home after good work from fellow signing Maxence Lacroix – and Joao Pedro returned the favour in the second period for Palmer, who netted his first of the campaign from an acute angle. Their goals proved decisive, with the Blues coming away from our west London neighbours with a 3-2 victory. And Alonso, while insisting he would not construct a team around the trio, emphasised what Palmer, Joao Pedro and Rogers can bring to the Chelsea side. He said: ‘They are going to be a very important part, but to build around them, no, it’s to build a team with them. They need to take responsibility, they need to lead the rest, they need to inspire the rest, because if they do great, the others will follow. 'We need to use them in the best possible situations and we need to have good links to reach them and they need to help the team be solid. The three of them, they have played for the team and scored, and that’s always important for the forwards.’ Palmer’s display on the banks of the Thames was particularly encouraging. For much of the previous campaign, he struggled with injury. It inhibited his game, with the England international admitting he wasn’t sure from one day to the next whether he would be in discomfort. Yet against Fulham, having had the summer off, Palmer appeared back to his fluid best. He weaved effortlessly beyond challenges and, while scoring and fashioning chances for team-mates, was also hugely impressive without the ball. Naturally, Alonso was pleased for the Blues’ No.10, and highlighted the influence Palmer can have when enjoying his football. He said: ‘I am very happy for Cole because I have really enjoyed seeing him play with this dynamism, with this freedom, with this responsibility, helping the team, and feeling important. We need that for the team. If Cole feels this way, we will have a better team and a better Chelsea. 'I am happy for him that he enjoyed his game, and you can see that.’ Up next is our midweek Carabao Cup clash against Luton Town and Alonso's Premier League home debut against Brighton & Hove Albion. news.title: Morgan Rogers: An enjoyable debut!
news.body_en: As debuts go, that Chelsea one from Morgan Rogers wasn’t half bad. After his switch to Stamford Bridge from Aston Villa, the England international would have been itching to hit the ground running. So scoring and helping the Blues to victory over Fulham will certainly have helped. Our No.17 restored our lead at Craven Cottage, after Joshua King had cancelled out Joao Pedro’s opener – which came after just 32 seconds. Cole Palmer, a close friend of Rogers, made it 3-1 just after the break, before Gonzalo Garcia reduced the deficit for Fulham. In the end, the Blues took all three points and Rogers – who played a key role alongside Palmer in a number ten role for Xabi Alonso’s side – believes this victory was a good start, but just that: a start. He believes there are still many gears for us to go up. ‘It was a great game to play in,’ Rogers said with a beaming smile. ‘Obviously to score and help the team win, that’s everything that I wanted from a debut. ‘I thought the quality of our play was excellent and it was so enjoyable out there. Fulham is a difficult place to come to, and they played really well, but we had that fight, that grit and I think we were the better team on the night. ‘For me, we deserved the win and I’m really happy with how the game went.’ Rogers would have been keen to make an impression at his new club, following his summer switch from Aston Villa, and having arrived later than some of his team-mates due to his involvement at the World Cup, the attacker believes the best version of him is still to come. ‘I didn’t feel that sharp towards the end, I was a bit tired and that’s why I came off for the last 10 minutes,’ admitted Morgan. ‘I’ve felt really good in pre-season but I’ve not had much of a break due to the World Cup, so I wanted to keep myself fresh. ‘Coming to a new team, you don't want to come in sluggish and off the pace, so I tried to keep myself in the best shape as possible and I’ve tried to get up to speed as quickly as I can. ‘I still think there are more gears to go, and I've got to try and find them as quickly as possible because the games are coming thick and fast. ‘But as I said, I felt good out there and I enjoyed it.’ Up next is our midweek Carabao Cup clash against Luton Town and Xabi Alonso's Premier League home debut against Brighton & Hove Albion. Full match: Fulham vs Chelsea
'I could feel the excitement'
Rogers' speaks after debut win
Alonso: 'A very professional, solid performance with maturity'
news.body_en: Xabi Alonso believes his Chelsea side produced a ‘very professional, solid performance with maturity’ to defeat Fulham in our Premier League opener and send the Chelsea supporters home from Craven Cottage with ‘happy faces’. Our first top-flight match of the campaign didn’t disappoint, with the west London derby against our neighbours testing the Blues in a variety of different ways. We broke the deadlock after just 32 seconds when Cole Palmer flicked a pass to Joao Pedro, who produced a deft finish to put us ahead. Fulham hit back midway through the opening period via Josh King, but Alonso’s side went into the interval ahead when Morgan Rogers struck on his debut. Cole Palmer then netted soon after the restart and, despite Fulham pulling a goal back through Gonzalo Garcia, we held on to claim all three points. After our win, Alonso highlighted several areas for improvement for his side. Yet the Chelsea manager was pleased to start his tenure with a win that showcased many different qualities we will need throughout the season ahead. ‘It feels very good, for sure,’ Alonso said in his post-match press conference. ‘We know how tough it is to win any Premier League game, and any away Premier League game. We prepared for an intense game, and I feel it was a very professional, solid performance, showing maturity and managing the difficult moments. ‘We got the lead quite early, had chances to score the second one, but after the equaliser we were through ten minutes when we didn’t choose the right moments to press and the movements. 'We corrected this well and in the second half, we felt comfortable without the ball, controlling the game. It was a performance to build for the future. There are things to improve for sure, but it was a good first day.’ Alonso added: ‘[It’s important] to manage in difficult moments, not to lose this emotional control. We know the Premier League is fantastic because sometimes the games are out of your hands. 'You don’t control them, so the players on the pitch need to know how to manage it – it’s as important as the tactics being right. It’s a process but today we went through good moments on that and we need to carry on that.’ After the full-time whistle was blown at Craven Cottage, Alonso and his players made their way over to the Chelsea faithful who had made the short trip down the Fulham Road to support their side. The Spaniard believes such moments are important in building a connection between those on the pitch and those in the stands. He said: ‘We are happy to play our first Premier League game of the season. My first official Premier League game with Chelsea felt great; in this stadium with our fans at the end, celebrating with them. ‘I had the feeling before kick-off that they were excited and they were hoping to see a good performance from the team, a serious one, and one they could see that we gave everything and fought for everything. I saw happy faces in the end and it’s important to create this bond. It’s early days, first game, but a good one.’
